endorsements.quote: Addressing these requires a framework for ongoing monitoring, periodic revalidation and transparent reporting mechanisms.
Mitigating these biases through diverse datasets and continuous model validation is critical to ensure fairness and accuracy in healthcare AI, particularly in high-stakes fields like cardiology.
Transparency also extends to informing patients when AI is used in their care, promoting trust and informed consent.

unlisted_practices: Establish a centralized reporting system to track and respond to AI-related incidents, creating feedback loops between clinicians, regulators, and developers.
Establish a framework for auditing datasets and algorithms over time to monitor bias mitigation.
Establish clear protocols for managing drift, retraining models, and auditing adaptive systems.
Define qualifications, specialized training, and standardized certifications for individuals providing human oversight of high-risk AI systems.
Clarify the allocation of liability among manufacturers, hospitals, and clinicians in cases of AI system failure.
Provide clear boundaries between risk categories and a mechanism to periodically reclassify AI systems as technologies evolve.
Provide detailed sector-specific guidelines on acceptable transparency and interpretability for medical AI, including regulation of black-box models.
Provide additional EU support to under-resourced regions and harmonize implementation of the AI Act, MDR, and EHDS across member states.

screen.reason: This is a discussion and perspective article exploring the implications, gaps, and regulatory governance challenges of the European Union's AI Act for medicine and cardiology.
